Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you had an episode of loss of consciousness; can you describe exactly what happened right before you passed out, such as any warning symptoms like dizziness, nausea, or a strange smell?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)

text: The ECG and CBC results are normal, and I cannot accept the suggested diagnosis of a urinary tract infection as the cause of your loss of consciousness. Before we conclude, have you experienced any palpitations, chest pain, or shortness of breath during the episode? REQUEST TEST: Blood Glucose

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood glucose results are within normal limits, which rules out hypoglycemia as the cause. Have you noticed any recent changes in your vision, such as tunnel vision or blurring, or did you feel unusually hot and sweaty before fainting? REQUEST TEST: Carboxyhemoglobin level

speaker: Doctor
text: The carboxyhemoglobin level is normal, which rules out carbon monoxide poisoning. Have you witnessed any rhythmic jerking movements or tongue biting during the episode, and do you recall any events afterward? REQUEST TEST: Arterial Blood Gas; REQUEST IMAGES: Head CT

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: The Arterial Blood Gas and Head CT results are normal, ruling out metabolic derangements and structural brain injuries. Have you noticed any triggers such as standing up quickly, dehydration, or exposure to a crowded, poorly ventilated space prior to the event?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history; the timing of your loss of consciousness immediately after urination is a very specific clue. Did you notice any dizziness, lightheadedness, or nausea right before you passed out?

Have you been experiencing similar episodes after other physical exertions like coughing, sneezing, or straining during bowel movements?

REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram with Valsalva maneuver; REQUEST IMAGES: Carotid Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram with Valsalva maneuver: NORMAL READINGS; Carotid Ultrasound: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The echocardiogram and carotid ultrasound results are normal, which helps rule out severe structural heart or vascular causes. Given your age, male gender, and the specific timing of the fainting episode immediately after urination, do you notice any straining or feeling of pressure in your abdomen right before you lose consciousness?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope
